newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Banco do Brasil extends Proex credit lines - paper.
newsitem.headline: Banco do Brasil extends Proex credit lines - paper.

text.p: The Brazilian government will extend as of July the special Proex export financing credit lines to the production of export goods, a financial newspaper said.
Until now the $1 billion in Proex funds, which are administered by Banco do Brasil, have only applied to exports themselves.
In some cases, Banco do Brasil will be charging one percentage point a year above LIBOR for the new credit line, but the exact credit conditions still need to be defined, Gazeta Mercantil said.
Banco do Brasil Director Renato Naegele said a number of measures would be introduced to promote the use of Proex funds which are currently undersubscribed, Gazeta Mercantil said.
In 1996, only 25 percent of Proex pure financing funds were taken up and only 40 percent of Proex funds aimed at subsidizing interest rate differentials between Brazil and abroad, Gazeta said.
The measures include reducing to seven days the time for approving Proex financing and cutting to 48 hours the approval time for interest equalization funds, Gazeta said.
Another 134 products will also be added to the current list of 4,459 goods eligible for Proex funding, Gazeta said.
Of the total $1 billion in Proex funds, $310 million go toward financing and $690 million go toward funding the equalization of interest rate differentials.
Banco do Brasil expects the new Proex conditions to help increase Brazilian exports by seven billion reais ($6.54 billion) by the end of 1997, Gazeta said.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
